interpretation: This audit summarizes the matrix's declared evidence states. It does not infer causality, convert source layers into a common denominator, or treat a non-open status token as a completed end-to-end result.

themes.measurement_level: Person, consumer unit, product, household record
themes.next_required_test: Follow repeated price adaptations and financial-condition changes, then join a defined price or payment shock to spending, food security, debt, and recovery where units permit.

themes.measurement_level: Person, diary day, trip, worker, household
themes.next_required_test: Measure waiting, travel, care, paperwork, and service effort against the time or money they displace; ATUS and NHTS now make separate time and trip currencies explicit, while the cross-source layer keeps political availability as a downstream open arrow; distinguish time spent, desired, controlled, and displaced.

themes.measurement_level: Customer case, complaint, firm, state, sector
themes.next_required_test: Follow digital/offline access → narrative and effort → response → verified remedy or abandonment → switching, trust, or non-use in the same service episode; public API/schema and platform ledger audits now make the missing correction, repeat-effort, receipt, durability, and exit fields explicit; product-conditioned response and visibility are visible, but adequacy, account exposure, failed attempts, and later behavior remain open.

themes.measurement_level: User, respondent, account, transaction, platform, seller, source ecosystem
themes.next_required_test: Verify encounter, interpretation, action, data use, agency, and exit effects with independent platform or transaction records; the new records distinguish reported use, attention frequency, perceived control/privacy, institutional inquiry, short-run engagement, and actual exit, which remains unobserved.

themes.measurement_level: Worker, task, job, workplace, firm, respondent
themes.next_required_test: Pair system or benefit exposure with decision rights, schedule, pay, health, worker voice, household security, bargaining outcome, and whether material strain is associated with civic availability; the new records distinguish adoption, saved time, algorithmic management, formal representation, worker voice, and job-quality association, while the MEPS two-clock audit adds event-family-aligned R4/2 and R5/3 nonemployment levels and transitions; proxies are not causal work measures.

themes.measurement_level: Person, caregiver, household, health event, diary day, county, provider-shortage component, care-recipient roster
themes.next_required_test: Follow care or food need → price/coverage/travel → care, diet, and unpaid time → work, debt, health, family time, and unpaid support capacity; SHED adds care-foregoing persistence, while MEPS adds month-ordered prescription follow-up and coverage-conditioned event context; preserve household and non-household care networks as separate exposure routes, and do not treat either layer as claim-level continuity or recovery.

themes.measurement_level: Home, person, trip, ZIP/year, disaster event, county, firm
themes.next_required_test: Keep three clocks separate—asset value, protection cost, recovery capacity—then build the matched place panel: population change → labor/demand → firms, housing, services → unequal access and mobility → complaint/remedy, repair, staying, moving, or exit, with belonging and political response measured separately.

themes.measurement_level: Person, household, place, customer, worker, program episode
themes.next_required_test: Three-way and four-way person-month comparisons now test distribution and persistence across resources, race, tenure, work-limiting condition, child presence, and financial condition; WBNS adds immigrant-family perceived-risk non-use and material/child hardship contrasts; the CCES screen adds material/trust/action heterogeneity; direct caregiving, mechanism, remedy, and downstream outcomes remain open.

themes.measurement_level: Respondent, customer, survey wave, community, source ecosystem
themes.next_required_test: Measure the interpretation between material experience and action: attribution, dignity, blame, belonging, institutional trust, and changing norms; HTOPS adds same-ID material-to-judgment timing but no action or attribution endpoint; WBNS adds a bounded perceived-risk/non-use signal and family hardship context, but does not observe trust change or causal enforcement effects; the CCES layer remains a descriptive joint-proxy screen, not a causal bridge.

themes.measurement_level: Person, household, program spell, agency, place, census tract
themes.next_required_test: SNAP receipt is now compared with food security, work, race, disability, child presence, resources, adjacent-month transitions, recorded reasons, joint housing insecurity, and resource/job changes around transitions with uncertainty checks; SIPP adds next-month food-security severity beside energy assistance and utility difficulty, while LIHEAP separates reach from reported restoration; WBNS adds perceived-risk public-benefit non-use in immigrant families, but not eligibility or a verified agency episode; durable recovery, direct notices, effort, interpretation, remedy, and later action remain open.

themes.measurement_level: Respondent, source ecosystem, program episode, county, election, campaign/event
themes.next_required_test: SHED, CCES, ANES, Pew, CPS, and HTOPS now separate consumer adaptation, economic judgment, trust, source environment, civic action, turnout, registration, and participation barriers; HTOPS supplies same-ID material-to-judgment timing but no action, attribution, remedy, or recovery endpoint; WBNS adds protective non-use as an observed behavior under perceived immigration risk, not as civic action; subgroup heterogeneity is now visible in CCES, but joint proxies do not establish causality, and migration-specific exposure, attribution, belonging, and causal action path remain open.

themes.measurement_level: Firm, product, market, worker, owner, community, state, county
themes.next_required_test: Record when a firm decision shifts price, waiting, access, risk, or data among customers, workers, owners, public systems, and future users—and who can resist; the sector and state layers show that application volume, establishment flow, net-job intensity, entry, and exit diverge; the finance-capacity screen is contextual and non-causal, not a market-power estimate.

themes.measurement_level: Firm, defense award, datacenter, building, campus, grid, public system, sector, country
themes.next_required_test: Compare planned and realized capacity, ownership, power/water burden, data location, local skills, interoperability, provider switching, and realized public capability; the ledgers keep procurement, testing, acceptance, delivery, operation, and rate/governance response distinct; the local GIS layer measures incidence, not load, jobs, bills, or benefits.

themes.measurement_level: Sector, commodity, firm, defense award, infrastructure project, country
themes.next_required_test: Trace realized capacity and ownership into local distribution, state dependence, alliance leverage, strategic choice, and external response without inventing a household-to-state join; retain procurement, acceptance, operational use, governance response, and leverage as separate stages.
